chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Abu Jamilah, from Amr ibn Hurayth, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who said: 'If I speak to a relative of mine, then upon me is the walking to the House of God, and all that I possess in the way of God, and I am free from the religion of Muhammad.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He fasts for three days and gives charity to ten poor people.'

key_terms.الْمَشْيُ إِلَى بَيْتِ اللَّهِ: Walking to the House of God (referring to Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking a vow to perform Hajj and donate all wealth?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific expiation (kaffarah) for a conditional vow involving speech to a relative, replacing the grandiose promise of Hajj and total wealth with the more manageable acts of fasting for three days and feeding ten poor people. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of easing burdens in vows (*nadhr*) while maintaining their spiritual validity, distinguishing between the literal fulfillment of the vow's wording and the prescribed compensatory acts. The hadith underscores the balance between intention and practical execution in devotional obligations.
